definitions.explanation: The land along the edge of a body of water such as a river, lake, or sea.

examples.japanese: ボートを{岸|きし}に{着|つ}けた。
examples.english: I moored the boat at the shore.

examples.japanese: {川|かわ}の{向|む}こう{岸|きし}に{家|いえ}が{見|み}える。
examples.english: You can see houses on the other side of the river.
examples.notes: {向|む}こう{岸|きし} = the other shore/bank

examples.japanese: {岸|きし}に{沿|そ}って{歩|ある}く。
{子供|こども}たちが{岸|きし}で{魚|さかな}を{釣|つ}っている。
examples.english: The children are fishing on the shore.

examples.japanese: {泳|およ}いでいたが{疲|つか}れたので、{岸|きし}に{戻|もど}った。
examples.english: I was swimming but got tired, so I returned to the shore.

notes:
{岸|きし} means shore, bank, or coast. It refers to the land at the edge of water.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {岸|きし}に{着|つ}く (to reach the shore)
- {岸|きし}に{沿|そ}って (along the shore)
- {岸|きし}から{離|はな}れる (to leave the shore)

COMPOUND WORDS:
- {向|む}こう{岸|きし} (the opposite shore/bank)
- {川岸|かわぎし} (riverbank)
- {海岸|かいがん} (seashore, coast)
- {岸辺|きしべ} (waterside, shore)
- {対岸|たいがん} (opposite shore)

NOTE: {岸|きし} alone often refers to riverbanks; for seashore, {海岸|かいがん} is more specific.
